title: The Prophet and the Question of Succession — Part 166

sentences.en:
The Prophet could foretell that Abu Bakr was his successor, and that the
existence of the Caliph after him was necessary.

Therefore, he realized that he should protect Abu Bakr
as he would his own.
So, he took him with him so that Abu Bakr might not be caught by the enemy.

Such treatment was not
shown to any other Muslim.
This clearly proves his right to the caliphate in preference to others.

Well-Wisher: If you would look at the verse more objectively, you would see that your conclusion is
wrong.
Sheikh: Can you advance reasons against the conclusions that we have drawn?
Well-Wisher: I should like you to pass over this issue at the moment because speech breeds speech.
Some biased people may interpret our comments with ill will.
I do not wish to incite hatred.

One might
conclude that we wish to dishonor the caliphs, though the position of each individual is fixed, and it is not
necessary to make useless interpretations.

Be assured that reasonable argument does not breed contempt; it
removes misunderstandings.

Well-Wisher: Since you have used the word "evasive," I am constrained to reply, so that you may know
that I am not avoiding the issue.
I wanted to maintain the propriety of our debate.
